views.name: customer_transaction_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  rowid AS transaction_id,
  txn_date AS transaction_date,
  CASE
    WHEN txn_amount IS NULL THEN 0
    WHEN txn_type IS NULL THEN txn_amount
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit','cancellation','refund') THEN abs(txn_amount)
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','debit','payment','charge') THEN -abs(txn_amount)
    ELSE txn_amount
  END AS amount
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: All customer transaction event rows canonicalized to use transaction date, customer id, and signed amount (positive for credits, negative for debits). Include any necessary normalization of nulls/amount signs but do not aggregate. One row per raw transaction event.

views.name: calendar_months
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  printf('%04d%02d', year_val, month_val) AS month_key,
  date(year_val || '-' || month_val || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  date(date(year_val || '-' || month_val || '-01'), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  year_val AS year,
  month_val AS month
FROM (
  SELECT
    year_min + (n) / 12 AS year_val,
    ((n) % 12) + 1 AS month_val
  FROM (
    SELECT
      CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS year_min,
      CAST(strftime('%Y', MAX(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS year_max,
      (CAST(strftime('%Y', MAX(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(txn_date)) AS INTEGER)) * 12
      + (CAST(strftime('%m', MAX(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', MIN(txn_date)) AS INTEGER)) AS months_span
    FROM (
      SELECT txn_date FROM customer_transactions
      WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
      UNION ALL
      SELECT market_date AS txn_date FROM bitcoin_prices
      WHERE market_date IS NOT NULL
      UNION ALL
      SELECT start_date AS txn_date FROM shopping_cart_users
      WHERE start_date IS NOT NULL
      UNION ALL
      SELECT txn_date FROM bitcoin_transactions
      WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
      UNION ALL
      SELECT week_date AS txn_date FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
      WHERE week_date IS NOT NULL
    )
  ), (
    SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
    UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17
    UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23
    UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
    UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
    UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41
    UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47
    UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53
    UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
    UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64 UNION ALL SELECT 65
    UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69 UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71
    UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74 UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77
    UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79 UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83
    UNION ALL SELECT 84 UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89
    UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94 UNION ALL SELECT 95
    UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99
  ) AS numbers
  WHERE n <= months_span
)
views.description: A canonical month dimension derived from transaction dates covering the full span of interest. Each row represents one calendar month (first_day, last_day, year, month_number, month_key). This ensures months with no activity can be joined later.

views.name: customer_monthly_activity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cte.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cm.month_key AS month_key,
  cm.year AS month_year,
  cm.month AS month_number,
  SUM(cte.amount) AS month_sum_amount,
  MAX(cte.transaction_date) AS month_last_txn_date
FROM
  customer_transaction_events cte
JOIN
  calendar_months cm
ON
  cte.transaction_date >= cm.month_start_date
  AND cte.transaction_date <= cm.month_end_date
GROUP BY
  cte.customer_id,
  cm.month_key
views.description: Monthly aggregated activity per customer: sum of amounts in that calendar month and the last transaction date within the month. This produces one row per customer-month where activity exists (aggregation only; months without activity are handled by joining with calendar_months).

views.name: customer_2020_transactions_filtered
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  txn_amount,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date >= '2020-01-01'
  AND txn_date <= '2020-12-31'
  AND (LOWER(txn_type) LIKE '%' || 'deposit' || '%' OR LOWER(txn_type) LIKE '%' || 'withdraw' || '%')
views.description: All customer transactions that occur within the year 2020 and that have a txn_type indicating either a deposit or a withdrawal (txn_type contains 'deposit' or contains 'withdraw', case-insensitive). This is a cleaned cohort filtered to the year and relevant txn_type values only.

views.name: customer_monthly_signed_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  substr(txn_date,1,7) AS month,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
    ELSE txn_amount
  END AS signed_amount,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Normalize transaction rows into a canonical month and signed_amount where txn_type determines sign: deposits positive, withdrawals negative. Also include a month identifier (YYYY-MM). Keep one row per original transaction with normalized fields.

views.name: customer_month_end_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) AS month,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      WHEN ct.txn_type = 'credit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
      WHEN ct.txn_type = 'debit' THEN -ct.txn_amount
      ELSE ct.txn_amount
    END
  ) AS month_end_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, substr(ct.txn_date,1,7)
views.description: Aggregate normalized signed transactions to compute each customer's month-level balance (sum of signed_amount) for each calendar month present in 2020. One row per customer per month.

views.name: monthly_customer_balance_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmb.month AS month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cmb.month_end_balance > 0 THEN cmb.customer_id END) AS positive_balance_customer_count,
  AVG(CAST(cmb.month_end_balance AS REAL)) AS average_month_end_balance,
  cmb.customer_id
FROM customer_month_end_balance AS cmb
GROUP BY cmb.month
views.description: For each month, compute metrics derived from customer month_end_balance: distinct count of customers with month_end_balance > 0 and the average month_end_balance across all customers who have at least one transaction that month.

views.name: customer_transactions_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date,1,10) AS txn_date,
  CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC) AS txn_amount,
  LOWER(COALESCE(txn_type, 'other')) AS txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND txn_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalize and filter customer_transactions rows: exclude rows with NULL txn_amount or NULL txn_date; parse/standardize txn_date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) and txn_amount numeric; canonicalize txn_type to lowercase and map NULLs to a default non-deposit value. Keep one row per original transaction.

views.name: customer_monthly_net
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
views.description: Aggregate normalized transactions to calendar month-level nets per customer: group transactions by customer_id and the month start date (first day of month derived from txn_date) and sum amounts with deposits treated as positive and all other txn_type values treated as negative.

views.name: customer_monthly_closing
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmn.customer_id,
  cmn.month_start,
  cmn.monthly_net,
  SUM(cmn.monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY cmn.customer_id ORDER BY cmn.month_start
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cmn.customer_id ORDER BY cmn.month_start) AS month_rank
FROM customer_monthly_net cmn
views.description: Compute each customer's monthly closing balance as the cumulative sum (in chronological order) of monthly_net per customer. One row per customer_id and month_start with closing_balance and month_rank/order.

views.name: customer_latest_and_prior_closing
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmc.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmc_latest.month_start AS latest_month_start,
  cmc_latest.closing_balance AS latest_closing,
  cmc_prior.month_start AS prior_month_start,
  cmc_prior.closing_balance AS prior_closing
FROM
  (
    SELECT customer_id, month_start, closing_balance, month_rank
    FROM customer_monthly_closing
  ) AS cmc
JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, month_start, closing_balance, month_rank
  FROM customer_monthly_closing
) AS cmc_latest
  ON cmc.customer_id = cmc_latest.customer_id
JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, month_start, closing_balance, month_rank
  FROM customer_monthly_closing
) AS cmc_prior
  ON cmc.customer_id = cmc_prior.customer_id
WHERE
  cmc_latest.month_rank = 1
  AND cmc_prior.month_rank = 2
  AND cmc.customer_id = cmc_latest.customer_id
  AND cmc.customer_id = cmc_prior.customer_id
GROUP BY
  cmc.customer_id,
  cmc_latest.month_start,
  cmc_latest.closing_balance,
  cmc_prior.month_start,
  cmc_prior.closing_balance
views.description: For each customer, find the most recent month (latest month_start) closing_balance and the prior month's closing_balance (if any). Produce one row per customer with columns for latest_month_start, latest_closing, prior_month_start, prior_closing.

views.name: raw_customer_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  txn_amount AS amount
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: All rows from the customer_transactions table with txn_date interpreted as a date; this is the canonical row-level transaction cohort used by downstream steps.

views.name: customer_txn_monthly_calendar
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS txn_month_start
FROM
  customer_transactions
views.description: Normalize transaction dates to month boundaries and compute the month (YYYY-MM-01) for each transaction and the transaction's calendar month start date; used to identify the chronological first month and to group by month.

views.name: customer_running_balance_by_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(ct.txn_date) AS as_of_date,
  (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t2.txn_amount), 0)
    FROM customer_transactions t2
    WHERE t2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND date(t2.txn_date) <= date(ct.txn_date)
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, date(ct.txn_date)
views.description: For each customer and date, compute the cumulative balance up to and including that date (running sum of transaction amounts ordered by txn_date). Provides the per-customer cumulative balance as-of any calendar date.

views.name: monthly_prior_month_customer_balances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- month_start_date: compute the calendar month start (YYYY-MM-01) from txn_date
  date(substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  customer_id,
  -- cumulative_balance_prior_month_end: sum of all transactions strictly before the month_start_date
  (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t2.txn_amount), 0)
    FROM customer_transactions AS t2
    WHERE t2.customer_id = t1.customer_id
      AND date(t2.txn_date) < date(substr(t1.txn_date,1,7) || '-01')
  ) AS cumulative_balance_prior_month_end
FROM customer_transactions AS t1
GROUP BY month_start_date, customer_id
views.description: For each customer and for each calendar month (month_start = YYYY-MM-01), produce the customer's cumulative balance as of the last day of the prior month. This uses the running balances to pick the balance on the prior-month-end for each month; rows for the dataset's first chronological month should be produced as baseline balances but months starting with that first month are excluded when returning final results (that exclusion is applied later).

views.name: customer_daily_transactions_aggregated
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_deposit,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type <> 'deposit' OR txn_type IS NULL THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_non_deposit,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_impact
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
views.description: For each customer and calendar date, aggregate transactions into total deposits and total non-deposit amounts and the net transaction impact for that date. This produces one row per customer per calendar date representing that day's aggregated transaction amounts.

views.name: customer_daily_end_of_day_balance_sequence
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  date(d.dt) AS date,
  IFNULL(r.cumulative_balance, 0) AS end_of_day_balance,
  CASE WHEN t.net_impact IS NOT NULL AND t.net_impact != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_transaction_day
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(txn_date) AS min_date, MAX(txn_date) AS max_date
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
) c
JOIN (
  -- generate calendar days for each customer between their min and max txn_date
  SELECT
    base.customer_id,
    date(base.min_date, '+' || (nums.n) || ' days') AS dt
  FROM (
    SELECT customer_id, min_date, max_date,
           julianday(max_date) - julianday(min_date) AS span_days
    FROM (
      SELECT customer_id, MIN(txn_date) AS min_date, MAX(txn_date) AS max_date
      FROM customer_transactions
      GROUP BY customer_id
    )
  ) base
  JOIN (
    -- numbers table 0..10000 (sufficient for typical spans)
    SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
    UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
    UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
    UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
    UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
    UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53 UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
    UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64 UNION ALL SELECT 65 UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69
    UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71 UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74 UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77 UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79
    UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83 UNION ALL SELECT 84 UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89
    UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94 UNION ALL SELECT 95 UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99
    UNION ALL SELECT 100 UNION ALL SELECT 200 UNION ALL SELECT 300 UNION ALL SELECT 400 UNION ALL SELECT 500 UNION ALL SELECT 1000
  ) nums ON nums.n <= CAST(base.span_days AS INTEGER)
) d ON d.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
  -- aggregated transactions per customer per date: deposits positive, others negative
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_impact
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
) t ON t.customer_id = d.customer_id AND date(t.txn_date) = date(d.dt)
LEFT JOIN (
  -- running cumulative balance up to and including that date per customer
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    r.as_of_date,
    SUM(r.net_on_date) OVER (PARTITION BY r.customer_id ORDER BY r.as_of_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      date(txn_date) AS as_of_date,
      SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_on_date
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id, date(txn_date)
  ) r
) r ON r.customer_id = d.customer_id AND r.as_of_date = date(d.dt)
views.description: Construct a complete chronological daily sequence for each customer from their earliest to latest txn_date, carrying forward days without transactions, and compute the end-of-day running balance per customer per date. Deposits add to the balance; any other txn_type subtracts. Starting balance is zero at each customer's earliest date.

views.name: customer_daily_30d_rolling_average_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.date,
  AVG(b.end_of_day_balance) AS rolling_30d_avg_balance
FROM customer_daily_end_of_day_balance_sequence AS b
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, date
  FROM customer_daily_end_of_day_balance_sequence
) AS d
  ON d.customer_id = b.customer_id
  AND b.date <= d.date
  AND DATE(b.date) >= DATE(d.date, '-29 days')
GROUP BY d.customer_id, d.date
HAVING COUNT(b.date) = 30
views.description: For each customer and date in their daily sequence, compute the trailing 30-day rolling average of end-of-day balances (including current day and prior 29 calendar days). Only produce rows where the customer has at least 30 days since their first date (i.e., the rolling window is full).

views.name: customer_monthly_max_30d_avg_excluding_baseline
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.customer_id,
  strftime('%Y', r.date) AS calendar_year,
  cast(strftime('%m', r.date) AS integer) AS month_number,
  MAX(CASE WHEN r.rolling_30d_avg_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE r.rolling_30d_avg_balance END) AS monthly_max_30d_avg_balance
FROM customer_daily_30d_rolling_average_balance AS r
-- exclude the customer's baseline calendar month (their first month that contains any transaction)
JOIN (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y', MIN(date)) AS first_year,
    cast(strftime('%m', MIN(date)) AS integer) AS first_month
  FROM customer_daily_30d_rolling_average_balance
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS first_months
  ON r.customer_id = first_months.customer_id
WHERE NOT (
    strftime('%Y', r.date) = first_months.first_year
    AND cast(strftime('%m', r.date) AS integer) = first_months.first_month
)
GROUP BY
  r.customer_id,
  strftime('%Y', r.date),
  cast(strftime('%m', r.date) AS integer)
views.description: For each customer and calendar month (derived from dates where a 30-day rolling average exists), compute the maximum of the 30-day rolling averages observed in that month for that customer. Exclude the customer's baseline calendar month (their first month that contains any transaction). Negative rolling averages should be treated as zero when computing the per-customer monthly maximum.
